lessons.title: Read guitar maps
lessons.focus: Chord-box orientation, TAB lines and fret numbers
learningObjectives: Explain or demonstrate the main idea: chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers.
Perform the target task accurately at a comfortable, controlled tempo.

explanation.keyIdea: Guitar TAB maps strings and fret numbers. The top line is the thinnest string (high E), the bottom line is the thickest string (low E), and a number tells you the fret to play; 0 means an open string. Staff notation is a parallel, optional way to represent pitch and rhythm.
explanation.plainLanguage: This lesson focuses on chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers. First understand the sound or movement, then practise a small part, then return to the musical whole. Treat the written checkpoint as an observable target, not a deadline.

demonstrationOrReference.referenceSuggestion: Use a clear, slow demonstration of chord-box orientation, tab lines and fret numbers from a reputable guitar-learning source or your own view of the fretboard. Compare the demonstration with the step-by-step guide here; no paid-course video or protected tab is reproduced.
steps: Check the tuning labels and identify the six string lines before playing.
Read numbers from left to right; stacked numbers are played together, while separated numbers are played in sequence.
For chord diagrams, read vertical lines as strings and horizontal spaces as frets; dots show finger locations and X/O mark muted/open strings.
